title: sre-weekly-update-2026-03-07
content:
SRE Weekly Update — week ending 2026-03-07

Owner: Ava Chen (eng-sre)
Collaborators: Liam O'Neill, Mariana Ruiz, Dev Patel
Status: in_review

Summary:
- This week focused on (1) mitigating a medium-severity incident affecting tokenization service, (2) SLO health review for hosted inference routes, and (3) improving on-call handoff docs and runbooks.
- No customer-facing outages; internal degradation windows occurred impacting batch tokenization for dedicated workloads.

Incidents:
1) Incident SRE-2026-03-03: tokenization-service degraded (medium)
  - Time window: 2026-03-03 03:42 UTC -> 2026-03-03 06:15 UTC
  - Impact: Increased latency and 5xx errors for batch tokenization requests on dedicated clusters; small percentage of hosted API inference calls experienced increased cold-start latency due to downstream backpressure.
  - Detection: Alert from tokenization-error-rate > 1% for 5 minutes (alert channel #sre-incidents).
  - Root cause (initial analysis): Regression introduced in recent tokenizer shard reconciliation change (PR #412) that caused excessive locking under certain request distributions leading to thread starvation on nodes with high small-batch traffic.
  - Mitigation: Rollback PR #412 on affected clusters (hotfix) at 04:05 UTC, temporary increase in replica count for tokenization service on dedicated pools, and a circuit-breaker rule added to upstream request router to fallback to single-shard tokenization for small-batch requests.
  - Post-incident actions:
    * JIRA: SRE-789 created to track full RCA and mitigation work (owner: Liam O'Neill).
    * Add unit + stress test to validate tokenizer shard reconciliation under skewed request mixes (owner: Mariana Ruiz).
    * Instrument additional metrics: per-shard queue length, lock hold time, and thread pool utilization (owner: Dev Patel).
  - Customer comms: No customer-facing downtime, incident summarized to customer-success for awareness.

SLOs / Metrics:
- Hosted API (text-generation route): 99.9% availability target (monthly). Current month-to-date: 99.94%.
- P50 latency: 120ms (target 150ms)
- P95 latency: 420ms (target 400ms) -> note P95 slightly above target; correlate with regional bursts on 2026-03-04 14:00 UTC (see spike chart on SLO dashboard).
- Dedicated inference SLO (throughput SLA for reserved pools): meeting SLA for committed throughput; observed two short windows where per-node CPU saturation reduced effective throughput by ~8% for <30 minutes during scheduled traffic ramp tests. Follow-up: tune autoscaling policy to be more aggressive on sustained 60s CPU > 70% (JIRA: SRE-791).
- Error budget summary: Hosted API error budget remaining: 78% this month. No automated burn mitigation needed currently.

On-call handoffs / Rotations:
- Last week's on-call: 2026-02-28 -> 2026-03-06: primary: Dev Patel, secondary: Mariana Ruiz.
- This week's on-call: 2026-03-07 -> 2026-03-13: primary: Maya Thompson, secondary: Aaron Kim.
- Handoff notes (from Dev -> Maya): see /confluence/sre/oncall/handoffs-2026-03-07 for full log. Key items:
  * Tokenization incident artifacts and current mitigations in progress (SRE-789).
  * Runbook update needed for tokenization fallback logic (owner: Maya).
  * Pager duty escalation thresholds temporarily lowered for tokenization-error-rate while extra instrumentation rolls out.

Runbooks and Playbooks:
- Tokenization service runbook updated with temporary rollback steps and circuit-breaker configuration. Need to add post-fix validation checklist (owner: Mariana).
- Autoscaling playbook: add guidance for dedicated-pool ramp tests and emergency scaling. Action item: record a short demo run for infra team (owner: Aaron Kim).

Meetings / Standups / Notes:
- Weekly SRE sync (2026-03-05): topics covered: tokenization incident recap, SLO health, upcoming DR drill on 2026-03-18, and plans for observability retention changes.
- Incident war room (2026-03-03): timeline created and pushed to JIRA SRE-789; key decision to rollback PR #412 within 20 minutes of escalation.
- On-call retrospective (2026-03-06): recommended improvements:
  * Improve pre-merge load testing for shard/locking changes.
  * Create synthetic small-batch traffic generator for integration tests.

Action items (short term):
- Mariana: add stress tests for tokenizer shard reconciliation (due 2026-03-20).
- Dev: implement per-shard queue and lock metrics in telemetry (due 2026-03-14).
- Liam: lead RCA writeup and schedule postmortem review (due 2026-03-10).
- Maya: update runbook with full rollback and validation steps (due 2026-03-09).
- Aaron: prepare autoscaling demo recording and propose updated policy (due 2026-03-15).

Risks / Blockers:
- Observability gaps: currently missing fine-grained per-shard lock metrics on production; blocks faster triage for similar incidents.
- Test coverage: changes to tokenizer core logic historically have low integration coverage for skewed traffic patterns.

Notes / Misc:
- Cross-team coordination: ask model infra and serving-runtime teams to review tokenization PRs touching shard reconciliation logic.
- Slack channels: #sre-incidents, #infra-tokenization, #serving-runtime.
- Related artifacts: JIRA SRE-789 (RCA), PR #412 (reverted), SLO dashboard (confluence link).

Planned work next week:
- Finish RCA and run postmortem review (Liam).
- Push instrumentation + metrics for tokenization (Dev + Mariana).
- Harden tests and merge new load tests (Mariana).
- Review autoscaling policy and roll out changes to dedicated clusters (Aaron).
- Run a DR drill focused on region failover for dedicated pools (schedule: 2026-03-18).

Attachments / Links:
- JIRA: SRE-789, SRE-791
- Confluence: /sre/slo-dashboard, /sre/oncall/handoffs-2026-03-07
- GitHub: github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-runner/pull/412

Quick wins / Requests for help:
- Ask platform-engineering to prioritize per-shard lock metrics in the next infra sprint (2-3 day effort estimate).
- Request model-infra to run a review on tokenizer PRs affecting reconcilers before merge.

End of update.

Notes to self: keep the weekly shorter next week; move detailed timelines to JIRA and link from here.
